comment: E1 cell map, Y3/Y4c/Y5/Y7 edition: every cell resolves to declared OpenGFX sprite ids (tools/opengfx-sprites.json, regenerated by `node tools/parse-pnml.mjs`) and every anchor is DERIVED from the declared xrel/yrel by the slicer — there are no hand-authored boxes, crops, tiles, compose blocks or anchors left in this file. Cell kinds: (a) plain declared ground tile (`sprite`, terrain_*); (b) `layers` — declared ground tile + declared building sprite(s) drawn at tileOrigin+(xrel,yrel), optional per-layer `tint` and `frames` for animation; (c) `trackset` — the 16 road/rail bitmask tiles built only from declared sprites (road = OpenGFX's finished flat tiles indexed through OpenTTD's flat table; rail = declared grass ground + declared rail overlay pieces); (d) `generator: highlight|highlight_soft` — the two procedural placement glows (UI, not OpenGFX art). Building cells keep the gameplay footprint (catchment/occupancy); the sprite sits on the footprint's south tile by construction, which is what makes its base land inside the footprint diamond (Y7). V1: the footprint is WHAT THE ART COVERS — every industry here is a single declared sprite whose ground tile is one diamond, so every footprint is [1,1]; validate-manifest.mjs now fails a building whose sprite is dramatically smaller than its footprint, so the two can never drift apart again.

sprites.name: terrain_grass
sprites.note: Y1: declared flat temperate grass (64x31, yrel 0). Single grass tile — the grass sheet is one type across a 19-sprite slope set, so there is no second flat variant (Y2).

sprites.name: terrain_rough
sprites.note: Y1: declared flat rough/rocky temperate tile.

sprites.name: terrain_water
sprites.note: Y1: declared water tile (4061, first frame used statically — OpenGFX animates water by runtime recolor).

sprites.name: farm
sprites.note: Y3: one declared building on its declared ground tile, placed by declared xrel/yrel (Y5/Y7).

sprites.name: ore_mine

layers.note: declared coal-mine ground tile (the one OpenGFX reuses for gold mine / factory stages)
declared coal-mine building (headgear + conveyor), 58x50 xrel -16 yrel -33

sprites.note: Y7: the ticket's own example pair — declared building on its declared ground tile sits flush on the footprint's south tile.

layers.note: declared gold-mine ground+conveyor tile, grey-tinted into a stone quarry

sprites.name: oil_rig
sprites.note: Y3: six declared animation stages as per-frame layers (one declared sprite per frame, per-frame width = the cell width) instead of the old 768x160 strip.

layers.note: declared gold-mine tile (ground + hut in one declared sprite)

sprites.name: factory_blue

layers.note: declared factory ground tile (clean concrete pad)
V2: declared complete works building (brick + two chimneys, 64x77), luminance-preserving player tint

sprites.note: V2: the factory is one declared sprite that is a COMPLETE building (2169). 2150 was one corner piece of OpenGFX's multi-tile factory and rendered as a sliver of chimneys; footprint is what the art covers (V1).

layers.note: declared grass ground so the 1x1 harvester sits flush on its tile (and the derived anchor stays inside the rect)
declared small shed building, player tint

sprites.name: road
sprites.note: Y4c: OpenGFX ships the complete flat road set at 1332-1350 (straights, curves, T-junctions, crossroads — finished 64x31 tiles). Each of the 16 masks is converted to OpenTTD RoadBits (toOpenttdRoadBits, src/iso/track.ts) and indexes OpenTTD's flat selection table; the declared sprite is blitted verbatim. The generator is gone.

sprites.name: rail
sprites.note: Y4c: OpenGFX's rail set is ground + per-piece overlays (1005-1010), not 16 finished tiles, so a mask draws the declared grass ground plus every declared overlay whose two directions are both set. Still fully declared — no generator, no mirroring.

sprites.name: crossing

layers.note: declared level-crossing tile (road+rail painted), drawn on tiles carrying both layers

sprites.note: Y4c: the crossing is the declared finished tile, not a centre-clipped extraction.

sprites.name: highlight_soft
sprites.note: U2: fainter catchment tint for the harvester's informational 4x4 area, distinct from the solid 1x1 placement tile.
